evidence.dominant_driver: August UK public-sector borrowing was £18.3bn, above the £15.5bn Reuters consensus and above every economist forecast, leaving April-August borrowing £8.1bn above the OBR path ahead of the October budget.

market_expectations.distribution_notes: Actual £18.3bn exceeded all Reuters-polled forecasts; year-to-date £77.3bn is £8.1bn above OBR projection.

observations.interpretation: The fiscal data is clearly worse than expected, but pre-open local market confirmation is absent and GBP is stable.

immediate.rationale: The FTSE cash market is still closed, so there is no valid 15-minute post-release UK100 reaction to confirm direction.

next_session.rationale: Persistent fiscal overshoot ahead of the October budget can keep a modest negative risk premium on UK equities if gilts cheapen.

15m.rationale: The FTSE cash market is still closed, so there is no valid 15-minute post-release UK100 reaction to confirm direction.

1h.rationale: The fiscal miss is negative, but before the cash open the direct index reaction is unavailable and GBP is not showing a disorderly move.

4h.rationale: Once London cash trading opens, the larger-than-expected borrowing gap can pressure domestic/rate-sensitive UK equities through fiscal-risk and future-tax expectations.

next_session.rationale: Persistent fiscal overshoot ahead of the October budget can keep a modest negative risk premium on UK equities if gilts cheapen.

predictions.mechanism: Worse borrowing raises UK fiscal-risk, gilt-supply and potential future tax-tightening concerns, which can weigh on domestic and rate-sensitive equities.
predictions.invalidation: If London opens with gilt yields stable/falling and UK100 holds above the prior close despite the fiscal miss, the 4h/next-session bearish thesis weakens materially.
predictions.counter_case: The miss may be treated as budget-specific rather than a growth shock; a strong global risk-on tape and the FTSE's multinational earnings mix can overwhelm domestic fiscal concerns.
